newsitem.title: USA: California bill would crack down on drunk drivers.
newsitem.headline: California bill would crack down on drunk drivers.

text.p: Drunk drivers who repeat the offence twice in California could lose the right to drive for the rest of their lives under a measure proposed Friday by a California state legislator.
In a twist on California's "three-strikes" law, state Assemblyman Tom Torlakson has proposed legislation that would revoke for life the license of drivers after three drunk driving convictions.
Torlakson, a Democrat, said he proposed the bill in response to recent accidents involving repeat drunk drivers.
"This bill is aimed at getting these habitually deadly drivers off the road," the assemblyman told Reuters. "It (the measure) could have a huge deterrent effect."
Each year, about 1,500 people in California die in alcohol-related accidents, according to the state's Department of Motor Vehicles.
Torlakson's drunk driving proposal would be modelled after California's existing "three-strikes" anti-crime law, which mandates stiff prison sentences for repeat offenders.
